result:
In `pricebook.py`, 12 of the 150 rules didn't match their docstrings. All 12 are fixed. Afterwards I ran all 150 rules against a reference implementation built from the docstrings, using a grid of quantities and unit prices plus negative-input checks, and found 0 mismatches.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 04, 07, 58 | The cap only applied once the discount went over twice the cap (e.g. `if disc > 100000`) | The cap now always applies |
| 15 | Threshold was `qty >= 21` | Changed to `>= 20` |
| 41 | Threshold was `qty >= 13` | Changed to `>= 12` |
| 66 | Threshold was `qty > 12` | Changed to `>= 12` |
| 16, 117 | The cap was applied to the price of the units above the threshold, not to the discount | Work out the discount first, then cap it |
| 21 | A "marginal" rule was discounting every unit | Now discounts only `(qty - 12)` units |
| 59, 72 | Used `round()`, which rounds to the nearest won | Changed to `//` (rounds down, as the common rules say) |
| 136 | Docstring says 5% but the code used 6% | Changed to 5% |

STATUS: DONE
